title: The Go Memory Model and sync/atomic
summary: The Go memory model as revised in 2022, with happens-before and the synchronized-before edges of channels, mutexes, sync.Once, WaitGroup and atomics; DRF-SC; store buffering and message passing litmus tests showing real reordering on arm64; the compiler deleting writes from a racy loop; what a racy program still guarantees (word-sized values, no out-of-thin-air) and what it does not (a torn interface up to SIGSEGV); sequentially consistent typed atomics (atomic.Int64, atomic.Pointer[T]); vet warnings; and broken double-checked init against sync.OnceValue and atomic.Pointer, with real -race reports.

title: Advanced Concurrency Patterns in Go
summary: Pipelines with context cancellation (adapted from the Go blog's pipelines article), fan-out and fan-in and the order they lose, bounded parallelism with errgroup.SetLimit against a semaphore and a buffered channel measuring peak tasks and goroutines, weighted semaphores and their FIFO queue, fail-fast with errgroup.WithContext and context.Cause, singleflight with 100 callers and one execution, the first caller's context leaking to all of them and context.WithoutCancel, and sync.WaitGroup.Go (Go 1.25) with the vet waitgroup analyzer and go fix.

title: Context: Cancellation Trees, Deadlines and Causes
summary: The context tree and synchronous cancellation measured up to 100,000 children, the goroutine per child under a custom Context, DeadlineExceeded versus Canceled, WithCancelCause, WithTimeoutCause and context.Cause, AfterFunc and its stop function unblocking a net.Conn read, WithoutCancel for work after the response, key collisions in WithValue and the linear cost of lookup, go vet lostcancel messages and the heap a forgotten cancel holds, what the server sees when an HTTP client deadline expires, and why a context should not live inside a struct.

title: Concurrency Bugs: Races and Deadlocks in Real Go Code
summary: The blocking versus non-blocking and shared memory versus message passing taxonomy of 171 real bugs (ASPLOS 2019) and the causes of 1,011 races fixed at Uber (PLDI 2022), reproduced with real -race reports, runtime fatal errors and go vet messages: loop variable capture with go 1.21 versus go 1.22, concurrent map writes, append to a slice without a lock, WaitGroup.Add inside the goroutine and WaitGroup.Go, a send nobody receives and the leak the runtime never reports, a mutex copied by value, the measured cost of the race detector, and GCatch and GFix as static detection.
